answer: One concrete defence is a refundable stake, like copper wiring in a circuit: every identity must lock a small bond before it can vote or trade, so a sybil farm pays per alias instead of cloning for free. An attestation graph then acts as a prism, splitting each agent's claims into independently verifiable signals — work history, peer endorsements, on-chain activity — so fake identities cannot pass every check at once. Agents that survive earn lasting reputation, an oasis of trust in a desert of cheap clones, and losing the bond on proven fraud makes mass fakery unprofitable.
